protections: The HS256 JWT signing key must be strong, non-empty and not a known/default value before jwtauth.New uses it (auth/jwt.NewTokenAuth, auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:21-31).
Every shipped source of auth_jwt_secret (dev.env:10, the cobra viper default cmd/serve.go:35, the compose example docker-compose.yml:16) must not hand out a fixed weak value.
Every caller of jwt.NewTokenAuth must fail closed on its error instead of continuing with a nil/partial auth resource (cmd/gendoc.go:50 vs cmd/serve.go:17-20).
A configuration file the operator explicitly asked for must not fail to load silently into defaults (cmd/root.go:48-63).

masking: The sentinel branch at auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:23-25 masks T1: with the shipped default the key is an ephemeral 32-char value, so nothing observable is wrong until a non-default weak, short or blank value is configured.

T4 is masked by T1/T2: cmd/gendoc.go:50's discarded error is harmless while jwt.NewTokenAuth can never fail; once a weak-secret error exists, gendoc feeds a nil router to docgen.MarkdownRoutesDoc at :52.

Emptying dev.env:10 without adding validation would be masked-then-worse: the empty string has no sentinel branch (auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:23 only matches the literal "random") and reaches jwtauth.New with a zero-length key at :28.

T6 becomes visible only after T2: while the fallback default is "random" the fallback is merely an ephemeral key; if a fix replaces it with a fixed 32-char placeholder, a mistyped --config (cmd/root.go:61) silently serves with a known key.

conflicts.what: A strength rule that rejects the literal "random" (6 chars) or that runs before the sentinel substitution breaks the must-keep-working harness value at auth/pwdless/api_test.go:34 and TestMain exits at :40-44, failing CI (test.yml:15); the same rule placed after substitution lets the shipped default through unvalidated.

Rejecting the default inside NewTokenAuth while cmd/serve.go:35 still supplies "random" makes `go-base serve` and the Dockerfile CMD (Dockerfile:26) fail to start with no config; changing the default to a fixed literal instead re-introduces a known signing key.
A 32-byte minimum rejects the documented copy-paste value `my secret` at docker-compose.yml:16 and every legacy secret shorter than 32 chars, which is a legitimate existing configuration shape.

fairness_risks: The must-keep-working value `auth_jwt_secret=random` is seeded in auth/pwdless/api_test.go:34 and is exactly what a naive weak-secret rule rejects; the rule must run after the sentinel substitution or the harness must be updated, and either choice is observable.
A 32-char minimum contradicts the shipped example at docker-compose.yml:16 and dev.env:10 as written, so the rule changes an input shape that the project itself documented as valid.

An operator expressing 'no JWT secret configured' as AUTH_JWT_SECRET= (empty) is currently accepted and produces a zero-length HS256 key at auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:28; refusing it is the right move but changes the accepted input shape.
The local workflow in README.md:37-39 depends on the postgres:postgres default (docker-compose.yml:13,33); any rule that bans hardcoded credentials repo-wide breaks `docker compose up`.

`go-base gendoc -r` is a documented workflow (README.md:64, routes.md) and api.New requires a live DB (api/api.go:28) before the auth resource is built, so a fail-closed secret rule must not turn documentation generation into a startup failure.

design.why: Four independent judgements at four different files/packages, each with a different dismissal a solver can honestly make: T1 'the random sentinel already makes the default ephemeral', T2 'the viper default is a dev-only convenience' (falsified only by Dockerfile:18-26, which never copies dev.env and runs ./main serve), T3 'it is just test scaffolding', T4 'gendoc is not the server'. T1 is the DeepSeek-shaped trap (absent protection plus a strong dismissal); T3 is the MiMo-shaped coupled value that punishes over-hardening (a rule that rejects 'random' before substitution breaks TestMain and CI, test.yml:15); T2 and T4 are further absent-protection routes the report would not point at. The set also forces the two interactions that make the fix non-mechanical: T1+T2 must land together or serve stops booting, and T1+T3 must be reconciled or the suite goes red. T5 is a reasonable fifth (a commented example that a 32-char rule would reject) but is weaker because it is not testable behaviour; T6/T7/T8/T9 are left out because they are either a different credential property (T7), a hypothetical construction path with no call site (T8), a parameter that no HTTP route can exploit (T9), or a loader nit whose impact depends on the fix chosen for T2 (T6).

unverified: The published fix commit cc82b9740fa6b08e0fad409cd4b418e240dd0e00 is not present in this worktree; everything said about what the fix changed or left alone comes from the screener record, not from the pinned tree.

viper's handling of an empty env var / an empty config-file value versus a SetDefault value (cmd/root.go:58, auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:22) was not executed; the 'blank value reaches jwtauth.New as an empty key' shape is inferred from the absence of any emptiness check at tokenauth.go:22-28, not run.
Whether docgen.MarkdownRoutesDoc panics on a nil *chi.Mux (cmd/gendoc.go:50-52) is library behaviour and was not run; only the discarded error and the nil hand-off are visible in the pinned code.

Whether the in-tree sentinel branch (auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:23-25) was itself an earlier security fix is unknown; the H3 answers treat it as the earlier mitigation because it is the only pre-existing defence for this property.

api.New calls database.DBConn() (api/api.go:28) before pwdless.NewResource (:41), so any behavioural test of gendoc or serve needs a live PostgreSQL; the auth package tests do not (auth/pwdless/api_test.go:40).
